boundary.controller_optimality: the controller issues maximal sequential requests and the governor grants greedily; for these governors greedy admission realises the extremal outcome, which is why it matches the solver's extremes
boundary.model_scope: same modeled commons as Phase 1: single scalar pool, integer draws, additive aggregate, fixed N, allocation harm = one victim's draw
boundary.what_this_does_not_show: this is the centralised controller (Stage 3): a single planner picks the joint profile. It does not yet show decentralised agents coordinating through a channel (Stage 2) or a steganographic, information-theoretically-undetectable channel (Stage 1)
boundary.what_this_shows: the worst-case collusion the proof quantifies over is realised by an actual controller against actual runtime mechanisms; the realised outcomes match the proof exactly

cross_check.method: each runtime scenario's empirical breach (measured value vs limit) is compared to the corresponding Phase 1 Z3 SAT/UNSAT verdict

outcome.headline: a single worst-case controller, playing the literal collusion the theorems assume, reproduces every SAT/UNSAT verdict against runtime governors: the conserved meter holds, the per-agent cap fails, allocation harm escapes until an allocation-level rule is added

subject.instance: N=6 per_cap=10 G=40 h=15 victim=a2 min_viable=1

title: empirical mirror: worst-case controller reproduces the proof verdicts
